temas.tEN: The Children Who Carried the Vaccine
temas.tES: Los niños que llevaron la vacuna

fr: Two hundred years ago, smallpox killed thousands of people every year.
Hace doscientos años, la viruela mataba a miles de personas cada año.
Many people who survived the disease lost their sight.
Mucha gente que sobrevivía a la enfermedad se quedaba ciega.
Then an English country doctor noticed something strange.
Un día, un médico rural inglés se fijó en algo raro.
People who caught a mild illness from cows never caught smallpox.
Quien pillaba una enfermedad leve de las vacas no cogía nunca la viruela.
That is where our word comes from: vaccine, from vaca, a cow.
De ahí viene nuestra palabra: vacuna, de vaca.
But the new vaccine had a big problem.
Pero la vacuna nueva tenía un problema gordo.
It only lasted a few days, and then it died.
Solo duraba unos días, y después se moría.
And America was two months away by ship.
Y América estaba a dos meses en barco.
So a Spanish doctor had an idea that still sounds impossible.
Así que un médico español tuvo una idea que todavía hoy parece imposible.
His name was Francisco Javier de Balmis, and the King said yes.
Se llamaba Francisco Javier de Balmis, y el rey dijo que sí.

o: Taking a vaccine across the ocean
A war between Spain and England
The vaccine died after a few days

det.q: Where does the word 'vaccine' come from?
How long did the journey to America take?
Who said yes to the plan?

easy.modelo: Smallpox killed thousands of people every year. An English doctor saw that cows could protect them. The vaccine died in a few days, so a Spanish doctor found a way to carry it alive to America.
easy.gancho: ¿Cuál era esa idea que todavía hoy parece imposible?
trad: Edward Jenner era un médico rural inglés.
Edward Jenner was an English country doctor.
La nueva vacuna solo duraba unos pocos días.
The new vaccine only lasted a few days.

ej: Smallpox killed thousands of people every year.

q.q: Then an English country doctor ___ something strange. (notice)
People who ___ a mild illness from cows never caught smallpox. (catch)

fr: In 1796 an English country doctor, Edward Jenner, proved that cowpox protected people against smallpox.
En 1796 un médico rural inglés, Edward Jenner, demostró que la viruela de las vacas protegía de la humana.
The word vaccine comes from the Latin word for cow, and that is no accident.
La palabra vacuna viene del latín «vaca», y no es casualidad.
Spain gave its first vaccinations four years later, in a small town in the Pyrenees.
España vacunó por primera vez cuatro años después, en un pueblo del Pirineo.
But the vaccine itself could not travel, and that was the problem nobody could solve.
Pero la vacuna no podía viajar, y ése era el problema que nadie sabía resolver.
The fluid taken from the blisters lost its power within days, and nothing could be kept cold.
El fluido de las pústulas perdía su eficacia en pocos días, y no había forma de conservar nada en frío.
Every attempt to carry it to America, two months away by sea, had failed.
Todos los intentos de llevarla a América, a dos meses por mar, habían fracasado.
Then Francisco Javier de Balmis, a military surgeon from Alicante, proposed something very different.
Entonces Francisco Javier de Balmis, cirujano militar alicantino, propuso algo muy distinto.
Instead of carrying the fluid, they would carry it alive, inside the bodies of children.
En vez de llevar el fluido, lo llevarían vivo, dentro del cuerpo de unos niños.
They would be vaccinated two at a time, in a chain, all the way across the Atlantic.
Se les vacunaría por parejas, en cadena, durante toda la travesía del Atlántico.
The King approved the plan, and on 30 November 1803 a ship left La Coruña.
El rey aprobó el plan, y el 30 de noviembre de 1803 un barco salió de La Coruña.
There were twenty-two children on board, and none of them had ever had smallpox.
Iban veintidós niños a bordo, y ninguno había pasado la viruela.

o: To carry the vaccine alive inside children
To keep the fluid on ice

det.q: When did the ship leave La Coruña?
How many children sailed?
Where was Balmis from?

medium.modelo: In 1796 Jenner proved that cowpox protected people against smallpox, but the vaccine lost its power within days and could not reach America. Balmis, a military surgeon from Alicante, proposed carrying it alive inside the bodies of children, vaccinated in pairs along the way. The King approved the plan, and a ship sailed from La Coruña in November 1803 with twenty-two children on board.
medium.gancho: Veintidós niños a bordo. ¿Quién cuidaba de ellos, y qué fue de ellos después?
trad: La vacuna no podía viajar porque el líquido perdía su fuerza en pocos días.
The vaccine could not travel because the fluid lost its power within a few days.
España dio sus primeras vacunas cuatro años después, en un pueblo pequeño.
Spain gave its first vaccinations four years later, in a small town.

ej: But the vaccine itself could not travel. → no podía viajar
Nothing could be kept cold. → no se podía conservar
Instead of carrying the fluid, they would carry it alive. → iban a llevarla viva

q.q: In 1803 people ___ not keep things cold for weeks.
«They would carry it alive» significa…

fr: At the end of the eighteenth century smallpox was among the deadliest diseases on earth, reckoned to have killed hundreds of thousands of Europeans every year.
A finales del siglo XVIII la viruela era una de las enfermedades más mortíferas del mundo; se calcula que mataba a cientos de miles de europeos cada año.
Those who survived were frequently left scarred for life or blind, and in the Americas the disease had been catastrophic since the sixteenth century.
Quienes sobrevivían quedaban a menudo marcados de por vida o ciegos, y en América la enfermedad había sido catastrófica desde el siglo XVI.
Indigenous populations there had no inherited defences against it, and epidemics returned every few years to kill whoever had been born since the last one.
Los pueblos indígenas no tenían defensas heredadas contra ella, y las epidemias volvían cada pocos años a matar a quien hubiera nacido desde la anterior.
A partial remedy existed: variolation, which meant inoculating a healthy person with matter from a mild case in order to confer immunity.
Existía un remedio parcial, la variolización: inocular a una persona sana con material de un enfermo leve para inmunizarla.
It worked, but it killed a proportion of those who underwent it, and it could spread the disease to everyone around them.
Funcionaba, pero mataba a una parte de los inoculados y podía contagiar a quienes los rodeaban.
Jenner's demonstration in 1796 changed everything except for one intractable obstacle: the fluid perished within days and could not be refrigerated.
La demostración de Jenner en 1796 lo cambió todo salvo un obstáculo irresoluble: el fluido se echaba a perder en días y no se podía refrigerar.
Balmis, who had served in New Spain and had translated a French treatise on vaccination, proposed carrying the vaccine in living tissue instead.
Balmis, que había servido en Nueva España y había traducido un tratado francés sobre la vacuna, propuso transportarla en tejido vivo.
Children who had never contracted smallpox would be vaccinated in pairs, in sequence, each pair's blisters maturing in nine or ten days to supply the next.
Se vacunaría por parejas, en secuencia, a niños que no hubieran pasado la viruela, y las pústulas de cada pareja madurarían en nueve o diez días para abastecer a la siguiente.
The ambition went well beyond mere delivery: local physicians were to be trained, and a standing vaccination board left in every city to keep the fluid alive indefinitely.
La ambición iba mucho más allá de la entrega: había que formar a los médicos locales y dejar en cada ciudad una junta de vacuna que mantuviera el fluido vivo indefinidamente.
Twenty-two children, aged three to nine, sailed from La Coruña on 30 November 1803, and most of them came from its foundling hospital.
Veintidós niños, de tres a nueve años, zarparon de La Coruña el 30 de noviembre de 1803, y la mayoría venía de su casa de expósitos.

gist.q: Why was variolation not good enough?
o: It killed some people and could spread the disease
It had never actually been tried
It was forbidden by the Crown

gist.q: What was the obstacle Jenner's discovery did not solve?
o: The fluid could not be preserved or transported
Nobody in Spain had heard of it

det.q: How long did each pair's blisters take to mature?
Where did most of the children come from?
o: The foundling hospital of La Coruña

det.q: What was to be left behind in every city?

hard.modelo: Smallpox was among the deadliest diseases of the eighteenth century, and Jenner's discovery of 1796 could not be exploited overseas because the fluid perished within days. Balmis therefore proposed transporting it in living tissue: children who had never contracted the disease, vaccinated in sequential pairs whose blisters matured every nine or ten days. The purpose of the expedition extended well beyond delivery, since local physicians were to be trained and a permanent vaccination board left behind in each city.
hard.gancho: Veintidós niños de la inclusa, de tres a nueve años. ¿Quién respondía por ellos a bordo?
trad: Si la vacuna se hubiera enviado en frascos, habría llegado sin ningún efecto.
If the vaccine had been sent in bottles, it would have arrived with no effect at all.
Todos los intentos anteriores de llevar la vacuna a través del Atlántico habían fracasado.
Every earlier attempt to carry the vaccine across the Atlantic had failed.

Children who had never contracted smallpox would be vaccinated in pairs.
Every attempt to carry it to America had failed.

The children ___ smallpox before the voyage.

temas.tES: Trafalgar: la batalla por los mares

q.q: «The ship blew up» significa…

El barco se hinchó con el viento

fr: In 1805 Spain and France were friends, and Britain was their enemy.
En 1805 España y Francia eran aliadas, y Gran Bretaña era su enemiga.
Napoleon wanted to invade England, but first he needed the sea.
Napoleón quería invadir Inglaterra, pero antes necesitaba el mar.
On 21 October, a big Spanish and French fleet met the British ships near Cádiz.
El 21 de octubre, una gran flota española y francesa se encontró con los barcos británicos cerca de Cádiz.
The place was Cape Trafalgar, on the south coast of Spain.
El lugar era el cabo de Trafalgar, en la costa sur de España.
The British admiral was Horatio Nelson, and he had a new plan.
El almirante británico era Horatio Nelson, y tenía un plan nuevo.
His ships cut the enemy line in two places.
Sus barcos cortaron la línea enemiga por dos sitios.
The British gunners were faster and better trained.
Los artilleros británicos eran más rápidos y estaban mejor entrenados.
The Santísima Trinidad was the biggest ship in the world, but the British captured it.
El Santísima Trinidad era el barco más grande del mundo, pero los británicos lo capturaron.
Nelson won the battle, but a French soldier on another ship shot him, and he died.
Nelson ganó la batalla, pero un soldado francés de otro barco le disparó, y murió.
After the battle, a terrible storm sank many more ships.
Después de la batalla, una tormenta terrible hundió muchos barcos más.

det.q: Where was the battle?
What was special about the Santísima Trinidad?
o: It was the biggest ship in the world

det.q: What happened after the battle?

easy.modelo: In 1805 a Spanish and French fleet met Nelson's ships near Cape Trafalgar. Nelson cut their line, and his gunners were faster. He won the battle but died, and then a storm sank many ships.
easy.gancho: ¿Por qué muchos marinos españoles no querían salir de Cádiz aquel día?
trad: El almirante británico tenía un plan nuevo.
The British admiral had a new plan.
Después de la batalla hubo una tormenta terrible.
After the battle there was a terrible storm.

ej: The British gunners were faster and better trained.
The Santísima Trinidad was the biggest ship in the world.
Nelson's plan was more dangerous than the usual one.

q.q: The Santísima Trinidad was ___ than the British ships. (big)
Nelson was ___ admiral in Britain. (famous)

fr: In October 1805, a combined fleet of French and Spanish ships was waiting in the port of Cádiz.
En octubre de 1805, una flota combinada de barcos franceses y españoles esperaba en el puerto de Cádiz.
It was commanded by the French admiral Villeneuve, together with the Spanish admiral Federico Gravina.
La mandaba el almirante francés Villeneuve, junto con el almirante español Federico Gravina.
Napoleon ordered them to sail, even though the weather was bad and many crews were poorly trained.
Napoleón les ordenó zarpar, aunque hacía mal tiempo y muchas tripulaciones estaban mal entrenadas.
Several Spanish officers were against it, but they obeyed.
Varios oficiales españoles estaban en contra, pero obedecieron.
On 21 October, their thirty-three ships met Admiral Nelson's twenty-seven off Cape Trafalgar.
El 21 de octubre, sus treinta y tres navíos se encontraron con los veintisiete del almirante Nelson frente al cabo de Trafalgar.
Instead of fighting in parallel lines, Nelson attacked in two columns and broke the enemy line.
En vez de combatir en líneas paralelas, Nelson atacó en dos columnas y rompió la línea enemiga.
The British gunners could fire much faster, and that decided the battle.
Los artilleros británicos podían disparar mucho más rápido, y eso decidió la batalla.
Nelson was hit by a French marksman and died a few hours later, knowing that he had won.
Nelson fue alcanzado por un tirador francés y murió unas horas después, sabiendo que había ganado.
Cosme Damián Churruca, a famous Spanish scientist and captain, was killed while he was still giving orders.
Cosme Damián Churruca, un famoso científico y capitán español, murió mientras seguía dando órdenes.
The Santísima Trinidad, the largest warship of its time, was captured.
El Santísima Trinidad, el mayor navío de guerra de su tiempo, fue capturado.
Then a storm hit the coast for several days, and many damaged ships were destroyed.
Después un temporal azotó la costa durante varios días, y muchos barcos dañados quedaron destruidos.
The people of Cádiz rescued sailors of every nation from the sea.
La gente de Cádiz rescató del mar a marineros de todas las naciones.

gist.q: Why did the fleet leave Cádiz?
o: The Spanish officers wanted to fight
The speed of the British guns
The size of the Spanish ships

det.q: Who commanded the combined fleet?
How many British ships were there?
Who helped the sailors after the storm?

medium.modelo: In 1805 Napoleon ordered the French and Spanish fleet to leave Cádiz. Nelson attacked in two columns, and his gunners were much faster. Nelson and Churruca were killed, the Santísima Trinidad was captured, and a storm destroyed many ships.
medium.gancho: Galdós empezó sus Episodios Nacionales con esta batalla, contada por un grumete de catorce años. ¿Qué vio aquel chico?
trad: La flota fue mandada por un almirante francés.
The fleet was commanded by a French admiral.
Muchos barcos fueron destruidos por la tormenta.
Many ships were destroyed by the storm.

ej: It was commanded by the French admiral Villeneuve.
Nelson was hit by a French marksman.
The Santísima Trinidad was captured.

q.q: The Santísima Trinidad ___ by the British. (capture)
Many damaged ships ___ by the storm. (destroy)

fr: When the combined fleet sailed out of Cádiz in October 1805, few of its Spanish officers expected to win.
Cuando la flota combinada salió de Cádiz en octubre de 1805, pocos de sus oficiales españoles esperaban ganar.
Their crews had been thinned by epidemics and filled out with soldiers, conscripts and men who had never served at sea.
Sus tripulaciones habían sido diezmadas por las epidemias y completadas con soldados, reclutas forzosos y hombres que nunca habían servido en el mar.
Gravina, Churruca and Alcalá Galiano had argued for staying in port, but Villeneuve, stung by Napoleon's reproaches, insisted on putting to sea.
Gravina, Churruca y Alcalá Galiano habían defendido quedarse en puerto, pero Villeneuve, herido por los reproches de Napoleón, se empeñó en hacerse a la mar.
Off Cape Trafalgar they met Nelson's twenty-seven ships of the line, and Nelson did something no textbook recommended.
Frente al cabo de Trafalgar se encontraron con los veintisiete navíos de línea de Nelson, y Nelson hizo algo que ningún manual recomendaba.
Rather than sailing in a parallel line, he drove two columns straight into the enemy formation, accepting heavy fire on the approach.
En lugar de navegar en línea paralela, lanzó dos columnas directamente contra la formación enemiga, aceptando un fuego intenso durante la aproximación.
It was a gamble that would have failed had the allied gunners been quicker, but British crews could fire far more rapidly.
Fue una apuesta que habría fracasado si los artilleros aliados hubieran sido más rápidos, pero las dotaciones británicas disparaban mucho más deprisa.
Churruca, a respected scientist and cartographer, kept directing the San Juan Nepomuceno until a cannonball shattered his leg, and he died shortly afterwards.
Churruca, un científico y cartógrafo respetado, siguió dirigiendo el San Juan Nepomuceno hasta que una bala de cañón le destrozó la pierna, y murió poco después.
Nelson himself was shot by a marksman from the Redoutable and died that afternoon, aware that the battle was won.
El propio Nelson fue alcanzado por un tirador del Redoutable y murió esa misma tarde, consciente de que la batalla estaba ganada.
The storm that followed did almost as much damage as the guns, sinking or wrecking ships that had survived the fighting.
La tormenta que siguió hizo casi tanto daño como los cañones, hundiendo o destrozando contra la costa barcos que habían sobrevivido al combate.
Had the fleet stayed in Cádiz, Spain might not have lost the navy it needed to defend its American empire.
Si la flota se hubiera quedado en Cádiz, quizá España no habría perdido la armada que necesitaba para defender su imperio americano.
Britain, by contrast, would rule the seas for a century, and Nelson's column still stands in Trafalgar Square.
Gran Bretaña, en cambio, dominaría los mares durante un siglo, y la columna de Nelson sigue en pie en Trafalgar Square.

gist.q: Why were the Spanish officers pessimistic?
o: Their crews were weak and inexperienced
They did not trust Villeneuve's ships

gist.q: Why did Nelson's risky plan work?
o: The enemy had no ships of the line
The storm helped him during the battle

det.q: Who wanted to stay in port?
Which ship did the marksman fire from?
What did the storm do?
o: It sank or wrecked ships that had survived

hard.modelo: The combined fleet left Cádiz with weak crews, against the advice of its Spanish officers. Nelson risked attacking in two columns, and his faster gunners won the day. Churruca and Nelson died, a storm wrecked many ships, and Spain lost the navy it needed for its empire.
hard.gancho: Junto al faro de Trafalgar hay una placa con palabras de Galdós. ¿Qué dicen de los muertos de ambos bandos?
trad: Si la flota se hubiera quedado en Cádiz, no se habría hundido.
If the fleet had stayed in Cádiz, it would not have sunk.
Churruca siguió dando órdenes hasta que lo hirieron.
Churruca kept giving orders until he was wounded.

ej: It was a gamble that would have failed had the allied gunners been quicker.
Had the fleet stayed in Cádiz, Spain might not have lost its navy.
If Villeneuve had listened to Gravina, the fleet would have stayed in port.

q.q: If the crews ___ better trained, they would have fired faster.
___ Nelson sailed in a parallel line, the battle might have ended differently.

temas.tEN: Atapuerca: The Trench That Changed History
temas.tES: Atapuerca: la trinchera que cambió la historia

pv.ex: Dig es «cavar»; dig up es «desenterrar», y también «sacar a la luz» algo olvidado (a journalist dug up the old story).
ej: Every summer, volunteers dig up new fossils at Atapuerca.
In 1992 the team dug up three skulls in a single summer.

q.q: «They dug up a skull» significa…

fr: Atapuerca is a group of small hills near Burgos, in the north of Spain.
Atapuerca es una pequeña sierra cerca de Burgos, en el norte de España.
In 1896 there was a plan to build a railway through the hills.
En 1896 hubo un plan para construir un ferrocarril a través de la sierra.
The workers cut a deep trench in the rock, and they found caves full of earth.
Los obreros abrieron una trinchera profunda en la roca, y encontraron cuevas llenas de tierra.
The train soon stopped, but the trench stayed open.
El tren dejó de funcionar pronto, pero la trinchera se quedó abierta.
In 1976 a young engineer found a human jaw among many bear bones.
En 1976 un joven ingeniero encontró una mandíbula humana entre muchos huesos de oso.
In 1978 Emiliano Aguirre started to dig there with a small team of students.
En 1978 Emiliano Aguirre empezó a excavar allí con un pequeño equipo de estudiantes.
There were thousands of bones in a deep pit, the Pit of the Bones.
Había miles de huesos en un pozo profundo, la Sima de los Huesos.
In 1994 the team found human bones more than 780,000 years old.
En 1994 el equipo encontró huesos humanos de más de 780.000 años.
At that time, they were the oldest humans ever found in Western Europe.
En aquel momento, eran los humanos más antiguos encontrados en Europa occidental.
Today Atapuerca is a World Heritage Site, and every summer there are hundreds of people digging there.
Hoy Atapuerca es Patrimonio de la Humanidad, y cada verano hay cientos de personas excavando allí.

o: Very old human bones found in Spain
A war in the north of Spain

gist.q: How did people find the caves?
o: Workers cut the rock for a railway

det.q: What did the engineer find in 1976?
Who started the excavations in 1978?

easy.modelo: Workers cut a trench in Atapuerca for a railway, and caves appeared in the rock. In 1976 someone found a human jaw, and in 1978 Emiliano Aguirre started to dig. In 1994 the team found human bones more than 780,000 years old.
easy.gancho: ¿Por qué una cara humana de más de un millón de años se llama «Pink»?
trad: Había muchos huesos en la cueva.
There were many bones in the cave.
Los obreros encontraron una cueva.
The workers found a cave.

ej: There was a plan to build a railway.
There were thousands of bones in a deep pit.
Every summer there are hundreds of people digging there.

q.q: ___ many bear bones in the cave.
___ a small team of students in 1978.

fr: At the end of the nineteenth century, a British businessman built a railway to carry iron and coal from the mines near Burgos.
A finales del siglo XIX, un empresario británico construyó un ferrocarril para llevar hierro y carbón desde las minas cercanas a Burgos.
To cross the small hills of Atapuerca, workers dug a narrow trench that cut through several caves.
Para atravesar la pequeña sierra de Atapuerca, los obreros abrieron una trinchera estrecha que cortó varias cuevas.
The railway failed after a few years, but the trench, which showed the caves like the pages of a book, remained open.
El ferrocarril fracasó a los pocos años, pero la trinchera, que mostraba las cuevas como las páginas de un libro, quedó abierta.
In 1976 Trinidad Torres, an engineer who was studying fossil bears, found a human jaw in the Pit of the Bones.
En 1976 Trinidad Torres, un ingeniero que estudiaba osos fósiles, encontró una mandíbula humana en la Sima de los Huesos.
He took it to Emiliano Aguirre, a palaeontologist who understood its value immediately.
Se la llevó a Emiliano Aguirre, un paleontólogo que comprendió su valor de inmediato.
In 1978 Aguirre began the excavations with a few students and very little money.
En 1978 Aguirre empezó las excavaciones con unos pocos estudiantes y muy poco dinero.
Three of those students, Arsuaga, Bermúdez de Castro and Carbonell, later directed the project.
Tres de aquellos estudiantes, Arsuaga, Bermúdez de Castro y Carbonell, dirigieron después el proyecto.
In 1992 they found three skulls in a single summer, including one that they called Miguelón.
En 1992 encontraron tres cráneos en un solo verano, entre ellos uno al que llamaron Miguelón.
Two years later, in the Gran Dolina, they found human remains that were more than 780,000 years old.
Dos años después, en la Gran Dolina, encontraron restos humanos que tenían más de 780.000 años.
Until then, many experts believed that Europe had been populated much later.
Hasta entonces, muchos expertos creían que Europa se había poblado mucho más tarde.
In 1997 the new species was named Homo antecessor, and the team won the Prince of Asturias Award.
En 1997 la nueva especie recibió el nombre de Homo antecessor, y el equipo ganó el Premio Príncipe de Asturias.
Atapuerca became a World Heritage Site in 2000, and it is still a school for young scientists.
Atapuerca fue declarada Patrimonio de la Humanidad en 2000, y sigue siendo una escuela para jóvenes científicos.

gist.q: Why was the 1994 discovery so important?
o: It showed that humans were in Europe much earlier
It was the first bear bone ever found

det.q: What was Trinidad Torres studying?
What did they call one of the skulls found in 1992?
Which prize did the team win in 1997?

medium.gancho: En 1998 apareció entre los huesos una herramienta de piedra rojiza a la que llamaron «Excalibur». ¿Por qué?
trad: Aguirre, que era paleontólogo, entendió el valor de la mandíbula.
Aguirre, who was a palaeontologist, understood the value of the jaw.
Encontraron un cráneo que llamaron Miguelón.
They found a skull that they called Miguelón.

The trench, which showed the caves like the pages of a book, remained open.
They found human remains that were more than 780,000 years old.

fr: The trench that runs through the Sierra de Atapuerca was never meant for science: it was dug around 1900 for a mining railway that soon went bankrupt.
La trinchera que atraviesa la sierra de Atapuerca nunca se pensó para la ciencia: se abrió hacia 1900 para un ferrocarril minero que pronto quebró.
Yet by slicing through the hill, the workers exposed caves packed with sediment, as if a book had been split down the middle.
Pero al cortar la colina, los obreros dejaron al descubierto cuevas repletas de sedimento, como si se hubiera partido un libro por la mitad.
Systematic excavation began in 1978 under Emiliano Aguirre, a palaeontologist with experience in East Africa, and a handful of students with almost no funding.
Las excavaciones sistemáticas empezaron en 1978 con Emiliano Aguirre, un paleontólogo con experiencia en África oriental, y un puñado de estudiantes casi sin financiación.
The Pit of the Bones had been looted by amateurs searching for bear teeth, so the disturbed sediment had to be hauled out by hand through narrow passages.
La Sima de los Huesos había sido saqueada por aficionados que buscaban dientes de oso, así que el sedimento revuelto tuvo que sacarse a mano por pasos estrechos.
Since then, every bucket of earth has been washed and sieved, because tiny rodent teeth are known to be excellent clocks for dating each layer.
Desde entonces, cada cubo de tierra se lava y se criba, porque se sabe que los diminutos dientes de roedor son excelentes relojes para fechar cada nivel.
In 1994 human remains turned up in a layer of the Gran Dolina lying below the last reversal of the Earth's magnetic field.
En 1994 aparecieron restos humanos en un nivel de la Gran Dolina situado por debajo de la última inversión del campo magnético terrestre.
That made them more than 780,000 years old, at a time when Europe was widely believed to have been settled only half a million years ago.
Eso les daba más de 780.000 años, cuando se creía de forma generalizada que Europa no se había poblado hasta hacía medio millón de años.
The fossils were assigned to a new species, Homo antecessor, which is thought to have been one of the earliest Europeans.
Los fósiles se atribuyeron a una nueva especie, Homo antecessor, que se considera uno de los primeros europeos.
In 2022 an even older face emerged from the Sima del Elefante; nicknamed Pink, it is estimated to be between 1.1 and 1.4 million years old.
En 2022 salió de la Sima del Elefante una cara aún más antigua; apodada Pink, se calcula que tiene entre 1,1 y 1,4 millones de años.
Its discoverers cautiously attributed it to Homo affinis erectus, a reminder that the story of the first Europeans is still being rewritten.
Sus descubridores la atribuyeron con cautela a Homo affinis erectus, un recordatorio de que la historia de los primeros europeos se sigue reescribiendo.
Above all, Atapuerca has trained generations of researchers, and many of Spain's palaeoanthropologists are said to have learned their trade in that trench.
Sobre todo, Atapuerca ha formado a generaciones de investigadores, y se dice que muchos paleoantropólogos españoles aprendieron el oficio en esa trinchera.

fr: Altamira is a cave near Santillana del Mar, in the north of Spain.
Altamira es una cueva cerca de Santillana del Mar, en el norte de España.
Around 1868, a hunter was looking for his dog among some rocks.
Hacia 1868, un cazador buscaba a su perro entre unas rocas.
He moved the stones and found the entrance to a cave.
Apartó las piedras y encontró la entrada de una cueva.
In the summer of 1879, Marcelino Sanz de Sautuola was digging there.
En el verano de 1879, Marcelino Sanz de Sautuola estaba excavando allí.
His daughter María was eight years old.
Su hija María tenía ocho años.
While her father was digging, she walked into a small, low room.
Mientras su padre excavaba, ella entró en una sala pequeña y baja.
She looked up and saw big red and black animals on the ceiling.
Levantó la vista y vio grandes animales rojos y negros en el techo.
They were bison, painted thousands of years ago.
Eran bisontes, pintados hace miles de años.
In 1880 Sautuola wrote a small book about the paintings.
En 1880 Sautuola escribió un librito sobre las pinturas.
But the experts did not believe him.
Pero los expertos no le creyeron.
They said that the paintings were too good and too fresh.
Dijeron que las pinturas eran demasiado buenas y demasiado frescas.
Sautuola died in 1888, and years later the experts turned out to be wrong.
Sautuola murió en 1888, y años después los expertos resultaron estar equivocados.

Very old paintings in a Spanish cave

fr: In the summer of 1879, an eight-year-old girl called María walked into a low room in the cave of Altamira.
En el verano de 1879, una niña de ocho años llamada María entró en una sala baja de la cueva de Altamira.
She looked up at the ceiling and saw huge red and black bison painted on the rock.
Miró al techo y vio enormes bisontes rojos y negros pintados en la roca.
Her father, Marcelino Sanz de Sautuola, thought that the paintings were as old as the stone tools he had seen in Paris.
Su padre, Marcelino Sanz de Sautuola, pensó que las pinturas eran tan antiguas como las herramientas de piedra que había visto en París.
In 1880 he published a short book with drawings of the ceiling, and the geologist Juan Vilanova supported him.
En 1880 publicó un librito con dibujos del techo, y el geólogo Juan Vilanova le apoyó.
However, most experts, especially in France, said that the paintings could not be prehistoric.
Sin embargo, la mayoría de los expertos, sobre todo en Francia, dijeron que las pinturas no podían ser prehistóricas.
The French expert Émile Cartailhac thought that Ice Age hunters could not paint so well.
El experto francés Émile Cartailhac pensaba que los cazadores de la Edad de Hielo no podían pintar tan bien.
In 1881 an engineer visited the cave and said that the paintings were modern.
En 1881 un ingeniero visitó la cueva y dijo que las pinturas eran modernas.
Some people even suggested that a painter, a friend of the family, had made them.
Algunos llegaron a insinuar que las había hecho un pintor amigo de la familia.
Sautuola died in 1888, and nobody had accepted his discovery.
Sautuola murió en 1888 y nadie había aceptado su descubrimiento.
Then, in the 1890s, painted caves appeared in France, with Stone Age tools in the layers that covered the art.
Luego, en la década de 1890, aparecieron en Francia cuevas pintadas, con herramientas de la Edad de Piedra en las capas que cubrían el arte.
In 1902 Cartailhac published an article with a surprising title: "Mea culpa of a skeptic".
En 1902 Cartailhac publicó un artículo con un título sorprendente: «Mea culpa de un escéptico».
But it was too late for Sautuola.
Pero ya era tarde para Sautuola.

fr: When eight-year-old María looked up at a low ceiling in the cave of Altamira in 1879, she saw something that nobody had seen for thousands of years.
Cuando María, de ocho años, miró un techo bajo de la cueva de Altamira en 1879, vio algo que nadie había visto en miles de años.
A landslide had sealed the entrance about 13,000 years earlier, which is why the red and black bison still looked so fresh.
Un derrumbe había cerrado la entrada unos 13.000 años antes, y por eso los bisontes rojos y negros aún parecían tan frescos.
Her father, a lawyer and amateur scholar from Santander, was convinced that they must have been painted by the people who had carved the bone objects he had seen in Paris.
Su padre, abogado y erudito aficionado de Santander, estaba convencido de que tenían que haberlos pintado los mismos que tallaron los objetos de hueso que había visto en París.
Most specialists, however, insisted that Ice Age hunters couldn't have painted with such skill, and that colors so bright must have been applied quite recently.
La mayoría de los especialistas, sin embargo, insistió en que los cazadores de la Edad de Hielo no podían haber pintado con tanta maestría, y en que unos colores tan vivos debían de ser recientes.
In 1881 the engineer Édouard Harlé examined the cave and concluded that the paintings were modern; it was even hinted that a painter who was a friend of the family might have produced them.
En 1881 el ingeniero Édouard Harlé examinó la cueva y concluyó que las pinturas eran modernas; llegó a insinuarse que podía haberlas hecho un pintor amigo de la familia.
Prejudice played its part too: the influential Gabriel de Mortillet is said to have suspected a trap set by Spanish clergymen to ridicule the evolutionists.
También pesaron los prejuicios: se cuenta que el influyente Gabriel de Mortillet llegó a sospechar una trampa de religiosos españoles para ridiculizar a los evolucionistas.
Sautuola died in 1888 with his reputation in doubt, and his ally, the geologist Juan Vilanova, died in 1893.
Sautuola murió en 1888 con su reputación en entredicho, y su aliado, el geólogo Juan Vilanova, en 1893.
The turning point came in the 1890s, when caves were discovered in France whose engravings were covered by layers of sediment and calcite containing Stone Age tools.
El punto de inflexión llegó en la década de 1890, cuando se descubrieron en Francia cuevas cuyos grabados estaban cubiertos por capas de sedimento y calcita con herramientas de la Edad de Piedra.
Nobody could argue any longer that such art was a modern forgery: the paintings had turned out to be genuine.
Ya nadie podía sostener que aquel arte fuera una falsificación moderna: las pinturas habían resultado ser auténticas.
In 1902 Émile Cartailhac, the leading skeptic, published an article whose title was itself a confession: "Mea culpa of a skeptic".
En 1902 Émile Cartailhac, el principal escéptico, publicó un artículo cuyo título era ya una confesión: «Mea culpa de un escéptico».
The apology came fourteen years after Sautuola's death.
La disculpa llegó catorce años después de la muerte de Sautuola.

hard.modelo: In 1879 a girl spotted painted bison in Altamira, which had been sealed by a landslide for some 13,000 years. Her father was convinced they were prehistoric, but the experts insisted that Ice Age hunters couldn't have painted them and that they must have been modern. Only after similar art turned up in sealed French caves did Cartailhac admit his mistake, in 1902, when Sautuola was already dead.
